a rhabdoid liver tumor in childhood is an extremely rare tumor with an aggressive course and poor prognosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a new class of rhabdoid tumors, which we have named "rhabdoid tumors with a glial component." The glial component is composed of cells which resemble the astrocyte and ependymal cells of the central nervous system.
we have shown that the rhabdoid phenotype can be produced in the absence of the hSNR5 gene, and that the hSNR 5 gene is not essential for normal development of the nervous system.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a child with an unresected liver mass and a high serum level VIP should be considered to have a VIPoma until proven otherwise.
